turn/pair: Take two entries of a query, a pair: two, one. Draw it as an arrow from the origin.
turn/turn: Rotating turns the arrow about the origin, keeping its length: a quarter turn, ninety degrees, carries it to minus one, two.
turn/unit: To turn any pair, start from an arrow of length one, pointing right, and turn it by the angle. Its tip lands at two numbers: across, the angle's cosine, written cos, and up, its sine, written sine.
turn/cossin: At ninety degrees the arrow points straight up: cos is zero and sin is one. At sixty degrees it lands one half across and about zero point eight seven up. Like e to a power, they are looked up, not worked out by hand.
rule/basis: So one, zero turns to cos, sin. And zero, one is one, zero already turned a quarter, so it lands a quarter turn past cos, sin. A quarter turn swaps the entries and flips the first sign, as two, one became minus one, two: minus sin, cos.
rule/rule: Any pair a, b is a times one, zero, plus b times zero, one. Turning moves both pieces, so it lands at a times cos, sin, plus b times minus sin, cos: a cos minus b sin, and a sin plus b cos.
rule/check: For ninety degrees: two times zero minus one times one is minus one, and two times one plus one times zero is two.
try/p: Try one. One pair of a key is one, one. What is it after a sixty degree rotation? Use cos sixty degrees is one half, and sin sixty degrees about zero point eight seven.
try/first: The first entry is a cos minus b sin: one times one half, minus one times zero point eight seven. About minus zero point three seven.
try/second: The second is a sin plus b cos: one times zero point eight seven, plus one times one half. About one point three seven.
try/done: So the pair turns to minus zero point three seven, one point three seven: the same length, pointing a sixth of a turn further round.
